what: runtime probe of the two (ptr, n) readings behind docs/06 42: the report layer reads `pos = pts[n-1]` at execute_results `0x472865`; each shot calls calculate_function TWICE (gw+3c30c7 / gw+3e2d3b) into two different buffers; is the array the report reads the same buffer, and are the two arrays bitwise identical?

build.address_space: RVA = ELF virtual address = module offset; Ghidra address = RVA + 0x100000

how.driver: tools/frida_point_array.py --attach   (NOT frida spawn: on this build spawn hangs the game in wait4 before it creates a window; see docs/06 42.1)
how.probe: tools/frida_point_array.js (read-only Interceptor hooks; no memory writes)
how.flow: Popen game -> attach -> click Campaign / level node / Start -> type f(x) -> LONG-PRESS Fire! -> execute_results
how.digest: FNV-1a 64 over ALL 16*len bytes of the point array (`digest_xy`) and over the y halves only (`digest_y`). Digests are only for indexing/recording: every same/different verdict is decided by an in-process byte-by-byte memcmp (cmpArrayBytes), not by a digest compare.
how.positive_control: the probe runs `selfTestCompare()` at install: two 100-point synthetic arrays, identical -> same=true; flip one bit at point 37 -> diffPoints=1 at index 37; flip another at point 90 -> diffPoints=2 at 37,90. Recorded in `probe_selftest`. A second, *runtime* positive control: shots with different f(x) do compare different (see `pair`/`vs` rows of shots across series).

cut: per shot: every calculate_function return record (ret addr, kind, ptr, len, both digests, first/last point), the byte-compare of call#2 against call#1, the execute_results queue snapshot (0x20-byte raw items + per-item len/ptr/digest/head8/tail8/classify), and the `movdqu` reading (rdx, rcx, n, the 16 bytes = pts[n-1], both digests, and its comparison against the queue snapshot and against both calculate_function arrays).
dropped: `beat` heartbeats, `reallocs` rows, `evals`/`samplers` bulk rows, and the full hex dump of each array (the raw JSONL has it; here only digests + head/tail points survive).
no_local_paths: this file contains no filesystem path and no user name; all pointers are ASLR-random per run.
notes: series1 (23 shots, one process, campaign Level 0): the f(x) box held 'sin(x)+3' with correction '+1.916' for the first group and 'sin(x)+4' with '+0.916' for the later group (read off the 1920x1160 UI frames). series2 (14 shots, another process): the box was retyped per shot with x/2 / 0 / sin(x)*2 / cos(x)-2 (frames show the text change), giving array lengths 1261 / 4473 / 5172 / 7066.

WITHIN a shot the two calculate_function calls (gw+3c30c7 and gw+3e2d3b, two different buffers) return BIT-IDENTICAL arrays in 37/37 shots. BETWEEN shots the arrays can differ by exactly +1 ulp at 1976/5441 points (never -1, x identical, first point identical): the series1 group switch is reproduced bit-for-bit by fl(fl(sin(x)+3)+1.916) (5440/5441 points, the single miss is index 0 = muzzle, which is not an evaluation) and the later group by fl(fl(sin(x)+4)+0.916) (5440/5441). Both are the same mathematical curve sin(x)+4.916; the 1 ulp comes from where the rounding happens, i.e. from a change of the (text, constant) representation, not from the point-array plumbing.

The report layer's movdqu (0x472865) always read the buffer returned by gw+3c30c7 (the graphwar_shot_calculator call that also fills the fire queue), never the gw+3e2d3b one; the queue snapshot taken at execute_results entry and the movdqu reading agree on (ptr, len, digest) in 37/37.

Operational traps hit while getting this far (see docs/06 42.1): (a) frida spawn hangs this build in wait4 before it creates a window - the driver now Popens the game and attaches; (b) the f(x) input box is at y~1090, not 1048; (c) 'mousemove X Y click 1' in one xdotool invocation dispatches the click at the OLD pointer position, so move and click/press must be separate invocations; (d) 'import -window root' is all black without a compositor - capture by window id.
